title: Channel or pair of channels violating p-norm multiplicativity for both some p>1 and some 0<p<1

decision.rationale: Hastings' peer-reviewed finite-dimensional gap at p = 1, combined with continuity of the minimum output Renyi entropy in p, yields a channel pair violating equation (26) on both sides of one, which is exactly what the archived statement asks for. The corroborating Leung-Lovitz-Wu manuscript was an unrefereed first version at the audit cutoff; the resolution does not depend on it.

source.title: Open problems in quantum information theory

formulation.notation:
| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $M_d$ | algebra of $d\times d$ complex matrices |
| $\Phi,\Omega$ | completely positive trace-preserving (CPT) maps (quantum channels) |
| $\Phi^{\otimes n}$ | $n$-fold tensor product channel |
| $\gamma$ | input density matrix (state), $\gamma\ge 0$, $\operatorname{Tr}\gamma=1$ |
| $\|X\|_p$ | Schatten $p$-norm, $\|X\|_p=(\operatorname{Tr}\lvert X\rvert^p)^{1/p}$ |
| $\nu_p(\Phi)$ | maximal output $p$-norm in the conventional formulation, $\nu_p(\Phi)=\sup_\gamma\|\Phi(\gamma)\|_p$ |
| $S^p(\gamma)$ | Standard Rényi $p$-entropy, $S^p(\gamma)=\tfrac{1}{1-p}\log\operatorname{Tr}\gamma^p$ for $p\ne 1$; $S^0(\gamma)=\log\operatorname{rank}\gamma$; $S^1(\gamma)$ is the von Neumann entropy |
| $S^p_{\min}(\Phi)$ | minimal output Renyi entropy, $S^p_{\min}(\Phi)=\inf_\gamma S^p[\Phi(\gamma)]$ |
| $p_1,p_2$ | two values of the Renyi/Schatten parameter, with $p_1>1$ and $0<p_2<1$ |
| eq. (26) | the multiplicativity/additivity assertion $S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega)$ |
formulation.statement:
**Problem 18 (Ruskai 2007).** Does there exist a quantum channel $\Phi$, or a pair of channels $(\Phi,\Omega)$ on finite-dimensional matrix algebras, and values $p_1>1$ and $p_2$ with $0<p_2<1$, such that the multiplicativity equality
$$S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega) \;=\; S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega) \tag{26}$$
**fails** at both $p=p_1$ and $p=p_2$? Equivalently, is there a single example that violates (26) simultaneously for some $p>1$ and some $p<1$?

If the answer is negative, then for every channel (pair) one can always approach $p=1$ from at least one side along which (26) does hold, which would force additivity at $p=1$.

question.summary: The source asked whether a single channel or channel pair can violate equation (26) simultaneously at some p above 1 and some p below 1. Hastings' fixed finite-dimensional additivity gap at p = 1, combined with continuity of the minimum output Renyi entropy in p, supplies such a pair.
question.importance: All known constructions were non-uniform in p, with the dimension blowing up as p approaches 1 and structurally different Kraus operators above and below one, and a negative answer would have forced a one-sided approach to p = 1 and reopened a route to the additivity conjecture there.

targetClauses.label: Simultaneous multiplicativity violation above and below p = 1
targetClauses.text: The archived statement asks whether there exists a quantum channel, or a pair of channels on finite-dimensional matrix algebras, and values p1 > 1 and 0 < p2 < 1 such that the multiplicativity equality (26) fails at both.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: A single channel or channel pair violating the identity on both sides of p = 1, or a proof that violation is always one-sided.

acceptedClaims.title: Hastings gap plus continuity in p gives a two-sided violation
acceptedClaims.text: Hastings produced a fixed finite-dimensional channel pair with a strict additivity gap at p = 1, and for fixed finite-dimensional channels the minimum output Renyi entropy is continuous in p at 1 because the state Renyi entropy is jointly continuous in state and order and the input-state set is compact. The strict gap therefore persists on an interval around one, and choosing one order on each side of one gives the single pair requested; Leung, Lovitz and Wu independently make this implication explicit and prove nonadditivity for every p > 3/4.

cautions.label: Scope
cautions.text: The solved label follows the source's explicit equation (26) for minimum output standard Renyi entropy; the continuity argument does not answer the different question of conventional maximal-output p-quasinorm multiplicativity for p < 1.
